title: A simple model of how the mind processes information
kicker: Inputs, thoughts, feelings and the models you use
blurb: A simplified model of how senses, feelings and thoughts feed one another, and why changing your inner models can change how the world feels.
description: A walk through a simplified, theoretical model of cognition. Senses and feelings are inputs, thoughts form a loop, and everything is shaped by your bodily state and by your verbal models of the world. The talk ends on how changing those models changes perception.
takeaways: Input comes from the senses and also from unconscious feelings, which can be seen as the body communicating with you.
Thoughts feed more thoughts, and what the mind turns to depends on what you have been thinking about before.
Processing is shaped by your overall bodily state and by your models of the world, which are probably verbal.
A kind word is processed through those models, may change how you see yourself, and can shift both feelings and what you do.
Whether rain or snow feels good or bad depends on your model, so you have some room to change how you see it.
